definition: Grouping images by visual similarity without labels, using learned representations.
details: Grouping images by visual similarity without labels, using learned representations. It enables dataset organization, deduplication, and unsupervised discovery.

explainer.lead: Image clustering groups images by visual similarity without labels, using learned representations. It matters for dataset organization, deduplication, and unsupervised discovery.

tiers.eli5: It is sorting a pile of photos into groups of look-alikes without anyone telling the computer what the groups are.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers extract learned representations and group images by similarity to organize or deduplicate datasets. Pitfall: with no labels, the discovered groups reflect representation similarity rather than any intended category.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as grouping images by visual similarity without labels using learned representations. The approach is unsupervised by construction.

explainer.example: A photo collection is grouped into clusters of visually similar images, letting near-duplicates be found and removed.
